svg.text: Logical Layers of the REST API - JobPortal BD
Node.js + Express 5, base path /api/v1. A request passes down through the layers; the JSON response travels back up the same way.
HTTP request from the React app - e.g. POST /api/v1/auth/login
any unknown path under /api/v1 answers with a JSON 404: { success: false, message: "No Api Found On This Route Location" }
reads the accessToken cookie, verifies the JWT
loads the user from MongoDB into req.user
no cookie / bad token / deleted user -> 401
PDF, DOC, DOCX | max 5 MB, kept in memory
collections: users, jobs, applications (connection string from MONGO_URI)
parsed request (req.body, req.cookies) enters the router
route-level guards run first: router.use(authMiddleware, roleMiddleware(role))
req.user set, role allowed, uploaded file available as req.file
calls helpers, sendMail, upload / delete file
Mongoose queries: find, create, save, delete
JSON response { success, message, ... } travels back up the same layers
- There is no separate service or repository layer: controllers call the utility modules and the Mongoose models directly, so Layer 5 is drawn as one band.
- Authorization is enforced on the server by roleMiddleware on the /applicant, /company and /admin routers. The frontend ProtectedRoute is only a user-experience redirect.
- Public routes (all of /auth except getme and updateprofile, and the job / company listing routes) pass through Layers 1 and 2 only and never touch the security middleware.
- Layer 1 also holds the global error handler (registered last); multer upload errors reach it and are returned as HTTP 400 JSON.
